concepts.name: zip for parallel iteration
concepts.description: zip() lazily pairs items from iterables in parallel; when equal lengths are required, strict=True turns a silent truncation bug into ValueError.

concepts.name: Unzipping with *
concepts.description: Passing *pairs to zip() expands the sequence of pairs into separate iterable arguments, effectively transposing rows into columns.

concepts.name: enumerate with explicit start
concepts.description: enumerate(iterable, start) yields index-value pairs without maintaining a manual counter.

concepts.name: Nested comprehensions
concepts.description: In a comprehension with multiple for clauses, the clauses appear in the same order as equivalent nested for loops.

concepts.name: Dictionary comprehensions
concepts.description: A dict comprehension writes key: value before the for clause and is useful for building lookup tables from objects.

concepts.name: next() with generator and default
concepts.description: next(iterator, default) returns the next item or the default instead of raising StopIteration when the iterator is exhausted.

concepts.name: Calling with *args
concepts.description: A leading * in a call expands an iterable into positional arguments for the target callable.

concepts.name: Calling with **kwargs
concepts.description: A leading ** in a call expands a mapping into keyword arguments, and ** inside a dict display merges mapping entries from left to right.

concepts.name: Dictionary ** unpacking precedence
concepts.description: Dictionary displays can unpack mappings with **, and later entries override earlier values for the same key.

concepts.name: Compound sort keys
concepts.description: sorted(..., key=...) can return a tuple so Python compares multiple fields lexicographically in priority order.

concepts.name: Assignment expressions
concepts.description: The := operator assigns a value as part of an expression so a computed value can be tested and reused without calling the function twice.
